title: Ampere force magnitude
description: Essential Criteria: The student must state the correct numerical value for the Ampere force, approximately 0.0693 N or exactly 4√3 × 10⁻² N.

title: EMF magnitude
description: Essential Criteria: The student must state the correct numerical value for the electromotive force, 4.0 V.

title: Force balance setup
description: Important Criteria: The solution must apply Newton's first law, balancing the component of gravity down the incline with the Ampere force up the incline.

title: Ampere force direction
description: Important Criteria: The reasoning must correctly determine that the Ampere force acts up the incline to oppose the component of gravity down the incline.

title: Current calculation
description: Important Criteria: The solution must relate the Ampere force (F = BId) to the current I, using the correct rail width d.

title: Circuit application
description: Important Criteria: The solution must apply Ohm's law to the complete circuit (E = I(R+r)) to find the EMF from the calculated current.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The solution should correctly convert all given quantities (mass, length) to SI base units (kg, m) before calculations.

title: Incorrect force component
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly uses mg sinθ or mg cosθ alone for the force balance instead of mg tanθ.

title: Neglecting internal resistance
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student uses E = IR instead of E = I(R+r), omitting the internal resistance r.

title: Direction/current sign error
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student misapplies the right-hand rule, leading to an incorrect direction for the Ampere force or current.
